hens_rule_text: Up to 5 hens are allowed per single-family dwelling with a City of Knoxville Urban Livestock Permit (one secondary source says 6, but the official permit application document states 5).
permit_notes: A permit from the Knoxville-Knox County animal services unit (administered with Young-Williams Animal Center) is required before keeping hens; a fee is charged. Permitted fowl are limited to single-family dwellings in R-1, R-2 or R-3 zoning districts.
setback_notes: The henhouse and fenced enclosure must be at least 10 ft from any abutting property line; the code text found does not give a separate distance specifically measured to a neighbor's dwelling.
coop_rules: No henhouse or enclosure is allowed in a front yard; must be at least 10 ft from abutting property lines; feed must be kept indoors or in a weather/rodent-resistant container and uneaten food removed daily.
zoning_notes: Only single-family dwellings in R-1, R-2 or R-3 zones are eligible for the permit; Tennessee has no statewide chicken law preempting city rules (a 2024 state bill on the subject died in summer study).
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: City of Knoxville Code of Ordinances, Animal Control chapter (exact section number not confirmed; permit governed via animal services rules)

sources.name: Application for Permit to Keep Domesticated Hens, City of Knoxville / Young-Williams Animal Center
Animal Control Permits, City of Knoxville

research_notes: Facts are drawn from search-engine text extracts of the official City of Knoxville hen-permit PDF and the city's animal control permits page, not from a direct read of the full PDF, since it could not be fetched as plain text in this session. The hen-count cap is inconsistent across secondary sources (5 vs 6); the number quoted directly from the official application document (5) was preferred.
